items.title: Add an iCIMS source: iCIMS career sites (Jibe JSON API) first
items.description:
## Problem

iCIMS is the largest job system we still can't read: 37 employers in the careers-page audit (#419), and the long-standing #173. iCIMS customers publish in one of two ways:

1. **iCIMS career sites** (iCIMS's "Jibe" product) on the employer's own domain (`careers.amd.com`, `careers.emory.edu`). These have a **public JSON API**:
   - `GET /api/jobs?page=N&limit=100&sortBy=posted_date&descending=true&country=<name>` returns `{totalCount, jobs: [{data: {...}}]}`;
   - each job has `title`, `slug`, `full_location`, `posted_date`, `employment_type`, `description`, `responsibilities`, `qualifications`, `apply_url` and `searchable`;
   - `country` takes a country name ("United States", "Canada", "India"), and `limit` goes up to 100;
   - the public job page is `https://<host>/jobs/<slug>`.
2. **Classic portals** (`careers-<company>.icims.com/jobs/search`): server-rendered HTML lists, with JSON-LD `JobPosting` on each job page.

This issue covers **(1)**. (2) follows in a separate PR into the same `icims` source.

## Probe (2026-10-15)

`/api/jobs` was tried on every unresolved employer's careers hosts. Seven are iCIMS career sites on iCIMS itself: AMD, PepsiCo, Medpace, First Citizens Bank, OHSU, Noblis and Emory.

S&P Global's and Mount Sinai's career sites also answer, but their `apply_url` points to Workday and Oracle HCM, which we already read. They're left out to avoid duplicating those boards.

Our filters would publish **226 curated jobs**: Emory 67, Medpace 51, First Citizens 38, Noblis 25, PepsiCo 23, AMD 22. OHSU publishes 0.

## Proposal

An `icims` source:
- one newest-first query per target country, bounded per country;
- postings de-duplicated by `slug`;
- `searchable: false` postings skipped, and `PART_TIME` dropped (owner rule, #390);
- the description built from the three HTML fields;
- errors reported as data.

`*.icims.com` portal URLs get a config error until (2) lands.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Adapter and tests with mocked HTTP.
- [ ] Registered, wired, with settings knobs and `validate_config` checks.
- [ ] The sites added after a live probe.
- [ ] A full real scrape exits 0 and passes `check_integrity.py`.

items.title: Add a SAP SuccessFactors (Career Site Builder) source
items.description:
## Problem

The careers-page audit (#419) found **51 employers** with recent entry-level US/CA/IN jobs whose job board is SAP SuccessFactors. It's now the largest job system we can't read (#316). Examples: Boston Scientific, Duke University, Leonardo DRS, NextEra Energy, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Teradyne, Westinghouse, State of Florida and State of Illinois.

## What SuccessFactors exposes

39 of the 51 run a **Career Site Builder** site on their own domain (`careers.duke.edu`, `jobs.bostonscientific.com`, …). There's no keyless JSON API: `/services/recruiting/v1/jobs` answers 401. But every site server-renders the same public search page:

- `GET /search/?q=&sortColumn=referencedate&sortDirection=desc&locale=en_US&startrow=N` gives rows with `a.jobTitle-link` (`/job/<slug>/<id>/`).
- The page uses one of two layouts:
  - **table**: `tr.data-row` with `span.jobLocation` and `span.jobDate`;
  - **tiles**: `li.job-tile` with `…-section-<field>-value` cells.
- Page size is 10–100 rows; a page past the end still contains `id="searchresults"`.
- Each job page carries microdata: `itemprop="datePosted"` (`Thu Oct 15 00:00:00 UTC 2026`), `addressLocality`/`addressRegion`/`addressCountry`, and the description in `span.jobdescription`.

The other 12 aren't covered here. Eleven use the legacy `career4.successfactors.com/career?company=…` portal, which needs a login flow. PG&E uses a Radancy (TalentBrew) front end.

## Proposal

Add a `successfactors` source modelled on Rippling (#398):

1. **List pass:** page the search, newest first, bounded by request count and `max_jobs_per_company`.
2. **Detail pass:** fetch the job page only for postings whose title passes `passes_title_rules` and whose list location is empty or in the US/CA/IN. That page supplies the date, a clean location and the description. Several sites show no date column, so without this pass their postings could never pass the recency rule.
3. **Location codes:** list locations look like `City, ST, CC, ZIP`. A naive reading takes Germany's `DE`, Morocco's `MA` and Malta's `MT` as US states (`is_valid_location("Schweinfurt, DE")` is True today). So the trailing ISO country code is rewritten: `US`/`CA`/`IN` become country names, and any other code makes the posting foreign.
4. **Errors are data:** a page without the search markup is a parse error, and a gone posting (404/410) is dropped.

**Prototype measurement** (2026-10-15, 39 sites, our filters): 534 curated jobs from 35 employers, with 316 detail requests.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Adapter plus tests with mocked HTTP: both layouts, paging, the detail pass, country codes, errors.
- [ ] Registered, wired, with settings knobs and `validate_config` checks.
- [ ] Boards added after a live probe, direct employers only.
- [ ] A full real scrape exits 0 and passes `check_integrity.py`.

items.title: Add 84 employer boards found on employers' own careers pages (Foorilla follow-up)
items.description:
## Problem

The Foorilla audit (#415) left 561 employers unresolved: their job boards weren't at a guessable slug on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable or SmartRecruiters. Most of them are large employers on Workday, Oracle HCM and other systems we already fetch. Foorilla doesn't expose their careers links.

## How the boards were found

1. Foorilla was re-read on 2026-10-15. Every company with at least 10 open jobs was checked (4,213 pages). Unconfigured employers with 3 or more recent entry-level jobs in the US, Canada or India were kept: 440 employers, after removing recruiters.
2. Each employer's **own website** was fetched: the homepage, `/careers`, `/jobs`, `careers.<domain>` and `jobs.<domain>`, plus links labelled careers or jobs. Their HTML was scanned for job-system URLs. A board linked from the employer's own careers page is strong evidence it belongs to that employer.
3. Workday tenants were confirmed through the CXS API, keeping the site with the most jobs. Other families were confirmed through their public APIs.
4. All 121 resulting boards were run through our own fetchers and `partition_jobs`, using the dash and senior-title fix from #417.

## Proposal

Add the **84 boards that publish 2 or more curated jobs, 1,102 in total**: 56 Workday, 15 Oracle HCM, 4 SmartRecruiters, 3 UKG, 2 Paylocity, and 1 each on Ashby, Greenhouse, Workable and Lever.

**Left out:**
- **Wrong board:** the link pointed at another company or region.
  - Deloitte → Deloitte Ireland
  - Toyota Automated Logistics → Vanderlande
  - ETAP → AVEVA
  - Argo Group → Brookfield
  - Emory → HHC
  - IKEA → IKEA Bulgaria
- **Staffing:** Diversified Services Network ("Staffing services to Fortune 500 companies"), under the direct-employers rule (#404).
- **Blocked:** Staples' Oracle HCM site answers 403.
- **Low yield:** 13 boards publish only 1 curated job, and 23 publish none.

**Not resolvable this way:** the families we have no adapter for were detected on 51 SuccessFactors sites, 37 iCIMS, 26 Phenom, 11 Avature, 11 Eightfold and 9 Taleo. 146 employers showed no job-system link at all. This tally is useful for #316.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Boards added; `validate_config.py` passes.
- [ ] A full real scrape exits 0 with no failed companies and passes `check_integrity.py`, with acceptable run time.
- [ ] README board counts are synced; `docs/removed-companies.md` is updated.

items.title: Filter: Unicode dashes hide co-op/part-time titles; senior 'Associate General Counsel/Professor/Dean' titles pass
items.description:
## Bug

Two title-filter false positives, found while measuring new employer boards on 2026-10-15.

**1. Unicode dashes defeat the hyphenated signals.** The signals are written with an ASCII hyphen (`co-op`, `part-time`), so a title with any other dash isn't recognised. Emerson's Oracle HCM board lists "Controls & Automation Engineering Co‑Op – Latham, NY - Summer 2027" (U+2011, a non-breaking hyphen), and our filters curate it as a full-time job instead of a co-op near miss. 216 live titles already contain Unicode dashes; none happen to hit a hyphenated signal yet, but Oracle HCM and Workday boards produce them routinely.

**2. Senior legal and academic "Associate …" titles pass.** "Associate" is a new-grad signal, so these are curated today:
- "Associate General Counsel" (Booz Allen ×3, Workday, IonQ, Roku, CoreWeave, Cloudflare)
- "Associate Professor" (Texas A&M ×8, Nebraska, UBC)
- "Associate Dean" (from new boards)

## Fix

- Fold Unicode hyphens and dashes (U+2010–U+2015, U+2212) to `-` in `passes_title_rules` and `classify_job`, before any rule reads the title. The published title is unchanged.
- Add `general counsel`, `associate dean`, `assistant dean` and `associate professor` to `filtering.exclusion_signals`.

**Effect on the live board:** 18 of 6,738 jobs drop: 8 "Associate General Counsel" and 10 "… Associate Professor" titles. "Associate Counsel", "Associate Software Engineer" and other junior "Associate" roles stay.

items.title: Add 54 direct-employer boards found by auditing Foorilla's hiring board
items.description:
## Problem

[Foorilla](https://foorilla.com/hiring/) lists about 247,000 open jobs from 22,721 hiring companies. An audit on 2026-10-14 found employers with recent entry-level jobs in the US, Canada and India whose boards are on a job system we already fetch, but who aren't in `config.yml`.

## How they were found

1. Every Foorilla company was listed (47,424). The 841 already configured were removed.
2. The Foorilla page of each remaining company with at least 5 open jobs (7,267) was read. Jobs were counted when they carry Foorilla's entry-level tag, are in the US, Canada or India, were posted within the last month, and are not internships, part-time or seasonal.
3. The 632 companies with 3 or more such jobs were probed on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable and SmartRecruiters, using slugs built from the name and website. A board was kept only if its job titles matched that company's titles on Foorilla. 71 boards matched; one (CGS Federal) is already configured.
4. The other 70 boards were run through our own fetchers and `partition_jobs`. **55 contribute curated jobs, 317 in total.**

## Proposal

Add 54 of them: 36 Greenhouse, 9 Lever, 7 Ashby and 2 SmartRecruiters.

**Left out:**
- **Vailexa:** it places contractors at client sites, so the direct-employers rule (#404) excludes it.
- **University Health Network:** some of its matches are "Casual" cleaner and aide jobs, which are close to the part-time roles the board excludes.
- **Pear VC:** a portfolio job board that posts for other companies.
- **Ten boards that contribute 0 curated jobs.**

**Not resolvable this way:** 561 companies, about 2,700 of the counted jobs. Most are large employers on Workday (KLA, PG&E, Walgreens, Supermicro, Sandisk, state universities). Foorilla doesn't expose their careers links.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Boards added, with display names taken from each board.
- [ ] `validate_config.py` passes.
- [ ] A full real scrape exits 0 with no failed companies and passes `check_integrity.py`.
- [ ] The README board counts are regenerated by `scripts/sync_readme_companies.py`.
- [ ] Additions and exclusions are logged in `docs/removed-companies.md`.

items.title: Add a Paylocity source adapter (9 verified direct employers)
items.description:
## Problem

**Paylocity** has 16 employers on the 30-day applied-jobs export (#390), and none of their postings reach the board. The backlog in #316 listed it as "no company id in the links", which this issue resolves.

## Evidence (probed 2026-10-14)

- **The export's links are job pages** (`recruiting.paylocity.com/Recruiting/Jobs/Details/<JobId>`). Each live job page links "View All Jobs" at `/Recruiting/Jobs/All/<company GUID>`, which is the company's board.
- **That board page embeds its full job list as JSON** in `window.pageData`, with no key. Each job has `JobId`, `JobTitle`, `PublishedDate`, a structured `JobLocation` (city, state, country), `IsRemote`, `IsInternal` and a `Description` snippet. There's no separate JSON API, so this works like the Google Careers source's embedded-data parsing.
- **Paylocity rate-limits bursts:** a quick probe received HTTP 429. One request per company and few workers are needed. GET requests already get urllib3's backoff and `Retry-After` handling.

## Companies

**Add (9 direct employers, every board probed live):** CU*Answers, Concept Solutions, E&M Technologies, Five Star Bank, Forgent Power Solutions, Interclypse, Oneida Professional Services, Trean, UNICO Group. Forgent appears twice in the export but is one board.

**Leave out (owner rule, direct employers only; see #404):** Abstrakt Marketing Group. The export's "Mechanical Comfort, Inc." link resolves to Abstrakt's board, which posts HVAC and sales jobs for client companies.

**Can't resolve:** CleanSlate Technology Group, Imagine, Northern Technologies Group, ES&S and Ryan Consulting Group. Their postings have closed ("Job Not Found"), so their links no longer reveal a company id.

## Proposed solution

1. Let `ngj.http.fetch_json_with_retry` hand back the raw text instead of JSON when asked, keeping the same cooldown and error handling.
2. Add `scripts/ngj/sources/paylocity.py`. It extracts `window.pageData` and skips internal and id-less jobs. Locations come from `JobLocation`, with remote marked once. Postings link to `/Recruiting/Jobs/Details/<JobId>`. A page without `pageData` is a parse error, so a layout change shows up in `health.json` instead of silently returning nothing.
3. Register the source (`apis.paylocity.companies: [{name, url}]`, where `url` is the board page). That covers the registry, pipeline, `Settings` (2 workers by default), `validate_config.py`, a 403-cooldown key per company GUID, README sync and the site's label.
4. Test with mocked HTTP only, then run a real local scrape and `check_integrity.py` before the PR.

items.title: Flaky test: contributors 'sponsor link only for handles with GitHub Sponsors' fails intermittently in CI
items.description:
## What happened

`site/src/components/contributors/contributors.test.jsx` › *sponsor link only for handles with GitHub Sponsors; profile is a real link* failed once in CI on PR #408, then passed when the failed job was re-run:

```
AssertionError: expected 'ambicuity' not to be 'ambicuity'
  106|     expect(sel()).not.toBe('ambicuity');
```

- Run: https://github.com/ambicuity/New-Grad-Jobs/actions/runs/38633101875 (first attempt failed, the re-run passed)
- PR #408 doesn't touch the contributors view or its keyboard handling.
- Locally the file passed 5 of 5 times, and recent `main` CI runs pass.

## Likely cause (not confirmed)

After `await screen.findByText(/SHOWN:/)`, the test presses `j` and checks synchronously that the selection moved. On a slow runner, either the window `keydown` listener (registered in an effect) isn't attached yet, or a later async update (contributors / GitHub enrichment resolving) resets the selection back to the first row after the keypress.

## Suggested fix

- Wait for the view to settle before the keypress, for example on the enriched roster.
- Assert the move with `await vi.waitFor(() => expect(sel()).not.toBe('ambicuity'))`, or press `j` inside `act(async …)` after the data promise resolves.
- Confirm the fix by running the file in a loop with CPU throttling (`--pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.singleFork`).

items.title: Watchdog: surface per-source health (status, failed companies, degraded/zero sources)
items.description:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/scraper-watchdog.yml` only checks how old `health.json` is (more than 3 h triggers a re-dispatch and a stale-data issue). It never looks at the per-source health that `health.json` already publishes: each source's `status`, `failed_companies`, and the top-level `degraded_sources` and `zero_sources`. A source that is quietly degraded, for example a provider blocking us or a schema change that zeroes a source, never shows up in the watchdog's run.

All 11 sources already share `ngj.http`: one session with urllib3 retries and backoff on 429/5xx for GET, per-source timeouts, the per-tenant 403 cooldown, and all-or-nothing handling of transient errors. So the gap is visibility, not inconsistent retry logic.

## Proposed solution

- Add a watchdog step that reads the same `health.json` and writes a per-source table to the job summary: source, status, jobs and failed companies.
- Emit a `::warning::` for every degraded or zero-job source, so it appears on the run without paging anyone.
- Keep the step informational, so it never fails the watchdog. Staleness remains the only trigger for re-dispatch and the stale-data issue, so behaviour doesn't change.
- Cover the summary logic with a test that runs the step's script against fixture `health.json` payloads.

items.title: Site: readable truncated cells, a skills fallback for unstructured descriptions, Explore CSV e2e
items.description:
## Problem

The board's site has three gaps, all verified against `main` on 2026-10-14.

1. **Truncated cells can't be read in place.** Desktop board rows (`JobRow.jsx`) and Explore rows (`ExploreView.jsx`) clip the company, role/title, location and source with `text-overflow: ellipsis`, and show no hover text. Long values such as "Anduril Industr…", "Waltham, Massachuset…" or "hosur road bangalore…" can only be read by opening the detail pane. Screen readers already get the full text from each option's `aria-label`; sighted mouse users don't.
2. **The requirements fallback is empty for unstructured descriptions.** `lib/requirements.js` only finds requirements under a header section or in a list of three or more `<li>` items. Plain-prose descriptions fall back to "None extracted from the description — see the full listing.", even when they name concrete skills (Python, C++, Kubernetes, AWS…).
3. **The Explore tab's EXPORT CSV has no end-to-end test.** `site/e2e/explore.spec.js` already covers presets, URL restore, tiers and keyboard selection, and `keyboard.spec.js` covers `/`, ↑/↓ and F2, but the CSV download is never exercised.

## Proposed solution

1. Give truncated cells a native `title` with their full value, in both the board and Explore.
2. Add a pure, unit-tested `lib/skills.js` that finds skill names from a fixed list as whole tokens in the description text. When no requirements list is found, show those names labelled **"Skills mentioned in the description"**, which is honest: they're derived, not invented. When none are found, keep the current message.
3. Add a Playwright test that clicks EXPORT CSV and checks the downloaded file's name, header and row count against the result count.

## Not in scope (already done; audit 2026-10-14)

- **Mobile layout** already switches below 1180px (not 768px) to single-column cards, a full-screen detail dialog and a FILTERS drawer, all covered at 375px by `mobile.mobile.spec.js`.

items.title: Add a Workable source adapter (5 verified direct employers)
items.description:
## Problem

**Workable** has 8 employers on the applied-jobs exports (#388, #390), and the scraper can't read it. It's the last job system on the backlog (#316) with a keyless public feed.

## Evidence (probed 2026-10-14)

- **The account widget needs no key:** `GET https://apply.workable.com/api/v1/widget/accounts/<slug>` returns the account `name` and every published `jobs` row in one response, with no paging. All 8 slugs answer HTTP 200.
- **Each row has** `shortcode`, `title`, `url` (`https://apply.workable.com/j/<shortcode>`, globally unique), `published_on`, `telecommuting`, `employment_type`, and a location (city/state/country plus `locations[]`).
- **The widget returns one row per location for the same posting,** like Rippling did (#400): Weekday AI has 1,054 rows for 724 postings, Credence 129 for 117. Rows must be merged by `shortcode`, combining their locations.

## Decision: direct employers only (owner, 2026-10-14)

Three of the 8 boards are recruiters posting for unnamed client companies, so the board would list the recruiter as the employer:

| Board | Curated jobs it would add | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Raydar (`raydar`) | 146 | talent network |
| Weekday AI (`weekday-1`) | 25 | hiring platform |
| Sapsol Technologies (`sapsol-technologies-inc-7`) | 6 | IT staffing firm |

They're left out, and this is logged in `docs/removed-companies.md`. The 5 direct employers are added: Credence, Texas Sports Academy, TP-Link Systems, Zifo and InterImage.

## Proposed solution

1. Add `scripts/ngj/sources/workable.py`, returning `SourceResult`. It makes one GET per account, merges rows by `shortcode` (combining locations), marks `telecommuting` postings remote, skips rows without a `shortcode`, and returns no partial jobs on a timeout or network error.
2. Register Workable as a board source (`apis.workable.companies: [{name, url}]`, where `url` is the widget API URL). That covers the registry, pipeline, `Settings`, `validate_config.py`, 403-cooldown keys by account slug (one shared host), README sync and the site's source label.
3. Test with mocked HTTP only, then run a real local scrape and `check_integrity.py` before the PR.

items.title: Add an ADP Workforce Now source adapter (3 verified tenants)
items.description:
## Problem

Three employers from the 30-day applied-jobs export (#390) post on **ADP Workforce Now**: Moran Environmental Recovery, Arcarithm and nou Systems. The scraper can't read that job system, so none of their postings reach the board. It's the last job system with a usable public feed, per the backlog in #316.

## Evidence (probed 2026-10-14)

- **The public career-center API needs no key or special header:** `GET https://workforcenow.adp.com/mascsr/default/careercenter/public/events/staffing/v1/job-requisitions?cid=<uuid>&$top=N&$skip=M`. It returns `jobRequisitions` and `meta.totalNumber`, and all 3 tenants answer HTTP 200, sorted newest first.
- **The server caps pages at 20,** whatever `$top` says. `$skip` is effectively 1-based (`meta.startSequence: 1`), so stepping by the rows returned repeats one row at the first page boundary. Stepping plus de-duplication by job id reaches every posting: 43 of 43 and 38 of 38.
- **Each requisition has** `requisitionTitle`, `postDate`, `requisitionLocations` (a `nameCode.shortName` like "Atlantic Beach, FL, US", plus an address) and `workLevelCode`. The posting's public id is the `ExternalJobID` custom field (e.g. `595411`), not `itemID`.
- **The posting page is `…/mdf/recruitment/recruitment.html?cid=<uuid>&jobId=<ExternalJobID>`,** which answers 200 and matches the export's links.

## Two cross-cutting gaps this exposes

1. **`canonical_url` keeps only `jobid`,** dropping `cid`. Two companies' postings with the same `jobId` would then share a `job_id`. The ids don't overlap across the 3 tenants today, but nothing guarantees that. `cid` should be kept **for `workforcenow.adp.com` only**: as a global rule, a generic `cid` (often a campaign id elsewhere) would split duplicates on other sites.
2. **Every tenant shares one host,** so the 403 cooldown would pause all ADP companies after one company's 403s. It must key on `cid`.

## Proposed solution

- Add `scripts/ngj/sources/adp.py`, returning `SourceResult`: paged GET, de-duplication by `ExternalJobID`, a cap per company, skipping requisitions without an id, and no partial jobs on a timeout or network error.
- Add a host-scoped query-id rule to `canonical_url` (`workforcenow.adp.com` → `cid`), and a query-parameter tenant key in the cooldown.
- Register the source (`apis.adp.companies: [{name, url}]`, where `url` is the career-center page with `cid`). That covers the registry, pipeline, `Settings`, `validate_config.py`, README sync and the site's source label. Add the 3 tenants.
- Test with mocked HTTP only, then run a real local scrape and `check_integrity.py` before the PR.

## Out of scope

**ADP MyJobs** (10 employers in the export) answers `400 Missing orgoid header`; each tenant's `orgoid` would have to be discovered first. That's tracked on #316.

items.title: Add a UKG Pro Recruiting (UltiPro) source adapter (19 verified job boards)
items.description:
## Problem

**UKG Pro Recruiting** (UltiPro) has 21 employers on the 30-day applied-jobs export (#390), more than any other job system still unsupported except iCIMS (backlog in #316). None of their postings reach the board.

## Evidence (probed 2026-10-14)

- **The public job-board search needs no key.** `POST https://<host>/<tenant>/JobBoard/<board-id>/JobBoardView/LoadSearchResults` with `{"opportunitySearch": {"Top": N, "Skip": M, "OrderBy": [postedDateDesc], "Filters": []}}` returns `opportunities` and `totalCount`.
- **All 19 boards in the export answer HTTP 200 with postings,** from the Cleveland Guardians (4) to Gray Media (504). The hosts are `recruiting.ultipro.com`, `recruiting2.ultipro.com` and `<company>.rec.pro.ukg.net`. Results sort newest first and pages don't overlap. `Top` accepts at least 500.
- **Each opportunity has** `Id`, `Title`, `PostedDate`, a `BriefDescription`, and `Locations` with a structured `Address` (city, state code, country). `LocalizedName` is often null, so the location must be built from the address. `JobLocationType` (null/0/1/2) does not reliably mark remote work: a "Remote / Virtual" posting has none, so the adapter doesn't use it.
- **The posting page `<board>/OpportunityDetail?opportunityId=<Id>` answers 200.**
- **Many tenants share `recruiting.ultipro.com`,** so the 403 cooldown must key on the tenant path, not the host.

## Proposed solution

1. Let `ngj.http.fetch_json_with_retry` take an optional JSON body, which sends a POST with the same cooldown and error handling. POST is not retried at the transport level, which is correct. Timeouts still get the board-level retry pass.
2. Add `scripts/ngj/sources/ukg.py`, returning `SourceResult`. It pages the search newest first, caps each board, builds locations from the address, skips postings without an `Id`, and returns no partial jobs on a timeout or network error.
3. Register UKG as a board source (`apis.ukg.companies: [{name, url}]`, where `url` is the job-board URL). That covers the registry, pipeline, `Settings`, `validate_config.py`, tenant-level cooldown keys, README sync and the site's source label. Add the 19 verified boards.
4. Test with mocked HTTP only, then run a real local scrape and `check_integrity.py` before the PR.

## Also probed (not in this issue)

- **ADP Workforce Now** (`careercenter/public/events/staffing/v1/job-requisitions?cid=…`): public JSON for the 3 employers on it. A small follow-up.
- **ADP MyJobs** (10 employers): answers `400 Missing orgoid header`. Not keyless as it stands.
- **Paylocity** (16): the export's links carry no company ID, and the ID found on one posting page returned an empty feed. Needs more digging.

items.title: [ROADMAP] Help us expand job data — all suggestions welcome!
items.description:
## TL;DR

We want to dramatically expand the job data this project surfaces, and we need **your ideas**. Whether you have a small tweak, a wild idea, or a full proposal — drop it in the comments. **All suggestions are welcome and I will reply to every comment.**

---

## Why this roadmap?

New-Grad-Jobs is most useful when it captures the widest possible surface of legitimate new-grad opportunities. Today we scrape and curate from a known set of sources, but there's a long tail of companies, regions, and job types we're missing.

This issue is the central place to brainstorm **how we add more jobs** — sources, regions, scrapers, partnerships, automation, data quality, anything.

## What kind of suggestions are we looking for?

Pick whatever resonates — these are just prompts:

### Sources
- [ ] Specific ATS platforms we don't yet scrape (Workday tenants, Greenhouse boards, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, iCIMS, Taleo, Eightfold, Phenom, Jobvite, BrassRing, etc.)
- [ ] Specific companies whose new-grad pipelines we should track
- [ ] Regional job boards (EU, India, LATAM, MENA, APAC, Canada, UK, etc.)
- [ ] University career portals worth aggregating
- [ ] Government / public-sector hiring portals
- [ ] Startup-focused aggregators (YC, Wellfound, etc.)
- [ ] Diversity-focused or accessibility-focused boards

### Job categories
- [ ] Internship pipelines distinct from full-time
- [ ] PhD / research / quant-specific listings
- [ ] Hardware, semiconductor, robotics, aerospace
- [ ] Game industry
- [ ] Finance / trading / actuarial new-grad tracks
- [ ] Bio / pharma / healthcare new-grad roles
- [ ] Trades, ops, supply chain, manufacturing new-grad programs

### Data quality
- [ ] How should we detect & dedupe reposted listings?
- [ ] How should we classify \"new grad\" vs \"junior\" vs \"intern\" more accurately?
- [ ] Should we surface salary data when available? From which sources?
- [ ] Should we flag visa sponsorship / remote / hybrid more explicitly?
- [ ] How should we handle stale postings (last-seen vs first-seen)?
- [ ] What metadata is most useful to filter on?

### Infrastructure & automation
- [ ] Scraper frameworks or libraries worth adopting
- [ ] Anti-bot / rate-limit strategies that respect ToS
- [ ] Workflow scheduling improvements (cron, GitHub Actions, queues)
- [ ] LLM-assisted parsing for unstructured careers pages
- [ ] Storage / dedup / canonicalization approaches
- [ ] Notification channels (RSS, Discord, Slack, email digest)

### Community & contribution
- [ ] How can we make it easier for contributors to add a new company in one PR?
- [ ] Should we publish a contribution template specifically for \"add a company\"?
- [ ] Would a structured YAML/JSON registry of companies + ATS endpoints help?
- [ ] Mentorship for first-time contributors who want to add a scraper

## How to suggest

Just comment below. Any format works:

- **A single company:** \"Please add `<Company>` — their careers page is `<URL>`\"
- **A source idea:** \"There's an ATS called `<X>` used by these companies: …\"
- **A feature idea:** \"It would be great if listings showed `<field>`\"
- **A full proposal:** longer-form design ideas, link to a gist or doc
- **A pain point:** \"As a job seeker, I wish this repo did `<X>`\"

You don't need to know how to scrape, write Python, or anything technical. **Ideas count just as much as code.**

## Commitment

- I'll **reply to every comment on this thread.**
- Concrete, actionable suggestions will be moved into their own tracking issues and linked back here.
- Larger themes will become milestones on the roadmap.
- Credit will go to the suggester in the resulting PR / issue / changelog.

## Ground rules

- Be respectful — this is a community space.
- Don't post anything that violates a source's Terms of Service or robots.txt; we want sustainable, ethical aggregation.
- Don't post personal data, recruiter contacts, or anything that could harm a company or candidate.
- Prefer one idea per comment when possible — it makes follow-up easier.

---

**Thanks in advance — every suggestion helps a new grad find their first job.**

`run_integrity_checks()` in `scripts/quality.py` is a key guardrail for publish safety, but several important failure paths are not explicitly regression-tested end-to-end.

Add targeted tests for scenarios such as:
- missing required artifacts (`docs/jobs.json`, `docs/health.json`)

Focus on deterministic, temp-directory-based tests only (no live network calls).

items.title: [Intermediate]: add deterministic test coverage for evaluate_jobs sidecar
items.description:
### 🧩 Intermediate Contributors
This issue is intended for contributors who already have experience with this repository
and the contribution workflow.

You should feel comfortable:
- Navigating `scripts/update_jobs.py`, `config.yml`, and `tests/`
- Understanding how `filter_jobs()`, `deduplicate_jobs()`, and `categorize_job()` work
- Following existing patterns without step-by-step guidance
- Writing non-trivial pytest tests with mocking

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must be assigned before starting** — comment `/assign` to claim this issue.
> PRs submitted without a prior assignment will be closed.

### 🐞 Problem Description
`scripts/evaluate_jobs.py` is part of the published analytics sidecar path, but it has little to no direct test coverage for:
- eligibility gating logic (`_is_eligible`)
- scoring heuristics (`_score_job`)
- output artifact shape and metadata consistency in `main()`

This creates risk that silent scoring/contract regressions ship unnoticed.

### 💡 Expected Solution
Add deterministic tests covering:
- `_is_eligible` include/exclude behavior for closed/malformed jobs
- `_score_job` score/confidence bounds and reason-code generation
- `main()` behavior with a temporary `docs/jobs.json` fixture, asserting generated artifact shape and key metadata fields

Keep tests network-free and deterministic. Do not change scoring policy in this issue.

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Problem is resolved per the description above
- [ ] Edge cases handled: None, NaN, empty string, Unicode, malformed data
- [ ] All existing `pytest tests/` pass
- [ ] New tests added for changed logic (deterministic — no live network calls)
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [ ] PR is linked to this issue with `Fixes #<number>`
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits format

### 🏗️ Which area does this touch?
🧪 Tests (tests/)

### 🔗 Additional Context
- Target module: `scripts/evaluate_jobs.py`
- Related contract helpers: `scripts/contracts.py`
- Related integrity checks: `scripts/quality.py`

items.title: [Advanced]: add iCIMS ingestion support to recover enterprise networking and infrastructure coverage
items.description:
### 🧠 Advanced Contributors
This issue is for contributors who are already very familiar with this codebase
and its architectural patterns.

You should feel comfortable:
- Understanding the full data flow: `config.yml` → fetch → filter → dedup → categorize → commit
- Reading and modifying `ThreadPoolExecutor` logic and thread-safety considerations
- Reasoning about API contract changes across ATS providers
- Writing rigorous, deterministic tests without live network calls

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You must be assigned before starting** — comment `/assign` to claim this issue.
> PRs submitted without a prior assignment will be closed.

### 🐞 Problem Description
The roadmap already calls out ATS coverage expansion as the biggest remaining quality gap. Today, the scraper has strong coverage for Greenhouse, Lever, Google Careers, and partial Workday, but it still misses entire slices of enterprise hiring that sit behind other ATS platforms.

iCIMS is a high-leverage next source because it is common among larger employers, including companies that post entry-level infrastructure, networking, and security roles that never reach the board today.

Without a first-class iCIMS integration, the dataset will continue to under-represent one of the main role families the README says it tracks.

### 💡 Proposed / Expected Solution
Add a production-ready iCIMS fetch path that follows the same project constraints as the existing sources:

- config-driven company definitions
- deterministic tests with mocked responses
- compatibility with the current normalization, filtering, and dedup pipeline
- no external database or browser-based dependency

This should be implemented as a source integration, not as a one-off company patch.

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A reusable iCIMS fetch path exists in the scraper
- [ ] `config.yml` can declare iCIMS-backed companies without custom code per company
- [ ] New source behavior is covered by deterministic tests with mocked payloads
- [ ] Thread-safety is preserved
- [ ] All existing `pytest tests/` pass
- [ ] New tests added for every changed code path (deterministic — no live network calls)
- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [ ] `jobs.json` schema remains backward compatible with `docs/app.js`
- [ ] PR is linked to this issue with `Fixes #<number>`
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits format

### 🏗️ Which area does this touch?
🤖 Core scraper (scripts/update_jobs.py)

### 🔗 Additional Context
- Roadmap reference: `ROADMAP.md` lists iCIMS support under v1.1
- Existing ATS references: Greenhouse, Lever, Google Careers, Workday
